findings.issue: A refused import (bad/forged signature, tampered container, package addressed to another device, newer format) writes no exchange_log row: ImportAsync throws CorrExchangeSignatureBad before the ExchangeLogEntry is added, and PreviewImportAsync writes nothing at all. As a result ExchangeLogEntry.SignatureOk is only ever stored as true, and the CoreAr.CorrExchangeSignatureBad branch of ListLogAsync is unreachable — an attempt to register a forged package leaves no trace anywhere in the product (the audit log is not written either). Covered by A_tampered_file_is_refused and A_file_addressed_to_another_device_cannot_be_opened_and_is_never_registered, neither of which asserts a log row.
findings.fix: In ImportAsync, before throwing on !read.Preview.SignatureOk, add an ExchangeLogEntry { Direction = InOutDirection.In, Kind = ExchangeKind.Msg, FileName = Path.GetFileName(path), OtherOrg = read.Message?.SenderOrgName, OtherOffice = read.Message?.SenderOfficeName, EntityId = null, SignatureOk = false, At = now } and SaveChangesAsync, then throw. Add a test asserting that after a refused import of a tampered file ListLogAsync returns one row with SignatureOk false and SignatureAr == CoreAr.CorrExchangeSignatureBad.

findings.issue: Residual shared-DbContext limitation the narrowed RollbackAsync cannot remove (the builder reported it in open_issues, and it is confirmed): SaveChangesAsync inside the numbering transaction flushes everything the session-scoped WakeelDb happens to be tracking, so a failed registration rolls those unrelated rows out of the database while RollbackAsync deliberately leaves their entities alone — an entity another screen had Added is left Unchanged and looks saved although its row is gone. Not introduced by this package: QuickCaptureService, InstallationService, HealthService and PhoneExpenseReview all open a transaction over the same shared context. The new test A_failed_registration_leaves_another_screens_unsaved_work_alone asserts only the part the narrowing controls (the rename survives, the added entity is not detached), which is correct and honest about its scope.
findings.fix: Architecture decision, outside this package: give the numbering transaction its own short-lived DbContext (a second WakeelDb built from the same connection string, or a dedicated factory) so the registration/approval writes only its own entities, and keep the session context untouched until it saves itself. Record the decision in ARCHITECTURE and apply it to the other four transaction sites at the same time.

findings.issue: SetStatusAsync applies any status to any referral with no guard: MarkAnsweredAsync on an already-Closed referral, or CloseAsync twice, both succeed and each writes a fresh CorrAuditReferralStatus audit row. The correspondence itself has a full transition table; the referral, which the same audit trail records, has none.
findings.fix: In SetStatusAsync, return the unchanged view without writing anything when referral.Status == status, and refuse with an Arabic sentence when the referral is already Closed and the target is Answered (a closed referral is reopened by a new referral, not by an answer). Add a test that answering a closed referral is refused and that re-closing writes no second audit row.

findings.issue: ApplyAsync refuses only an unnumbered row; a numbered letter that is Cancelled or Archived can still have its subject, party name, dates or body corrected. ReferralService.CreateAsync was given exactly this guard in round 3 (CoreAr.CorrRefusedReferralStatus) for the same reason — a withdrawn or filed letter is out of the office's hands — so the two commands now disagree about what a cancelled letter accepts.
findings.fix: After the OfficialNumber null check in ApplyAsync, refuse when row.Status is CorrespondenceStatus.Cancelled or CorrespondenceStatus.Archived, reusing CoreAr.CorrRefusedReferralStatus's sibling wording (a new CoreAr string naming correction rather than referral). Add a theory covering both states asserting the refusal is Latin-free and that no corrections row was written.

SPEC COVERAGE. Every B3-1 component in scope is implemented: CorrespondenceService (draft in/out, field validation, register-in with kind=in inside one transaction plus the party-name snapshot, the six-step outgoing wizard with the item-18 readiness checklist and an approval that issues the number and freezes the document, the eight states with a data-driven transition table, soft delete of an unnumbered draft, cancellation keeping the number with its reason, manual close with a note, archive, item 7, links, an audit row per transition), DuplicateDetector (exact party-number+party refused, same-number-other-party and Jaccard ≥ 0.8 on ArabicText-normalised words as reviews with «ليست مكررة»), ReferralService with the IDerivedDocumentBuilder contract defined here and the original never touched, FollowUpService (four kinds, next date, reminder, state change, «بانتظار رد منذ N أيام»), CorrectionService (both versions plus reason in corrections, two-pass so a partial batch can never be left on the tracked entity), ExchangeService (.wakeel-msg export sealed to the recipient key from the structure or the party profile with the org recovery copy, preview then import with internal/external numbering per items 49 and 22). Everything is registered in the Core DI extension, IReferralService through a factory so the optional builder resolves. TemplateService/LetterComposer are the next package and correctly absent.

SECURITY. Numbering happens only inside the two transactions, never on a draft, with ClockGuard consulted first and the verdict handed through; a failure after numbering rolls the sequence back and the next registration still gets 001. Cancellation keeps the number and stores the reason; a cancelled letter is refused for export. Container entry names are validated by ContainerEntrySource.IsAcceptableName on both write and read (ValidateShape), so a hostile package cannot smuggle a traversing attachment name through ExchangeService's `files/` stripping. No key, seed or password is stored, logged or held: DeviceIdentity is passed in by the caller per call and never captured. Every refusal sentence is Arabic with no error code.

QUALITY. Tests assert real behaviour throughout — duplicate detection is exercised on genuine Arabic subjects with diacritics, tatweel and the ة/ه and ى/ي spellings; the exchange round trip runs between two separately activated temporary installations with real certificates; the tampered-file and wrong-device cases are driven through the actual container. No test skips. No file outside the allowed paths was touched and no package was added. The four findings above are all low and none of them blocks the package.
